items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 53:1
items.html: It is known that the essence of Arich Anpin is two heads: the Galgalta and the Sealed Brain. But in terms of the division of the garments of the Mochin into the aspect of the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK of Tzelem, it is divided into three heads: the Galgalta, the Avir, and the Sealed Brain, as in Answer 15 above, see there. And just as the three heads are included one in the other, and in each of them the aspect of the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK of the three heads is discerned, as above, Page 312, Item 39, so too in the discernment of the two heads, they are included one in the other: in the head of the Galgalta there are a Galgalta and a Sealed Brain, which are Keter and Hochma, each having ten Sefirot. And likewise in the head of the Sealed Brain there are a Galgalta and a Sealed Brain, which are Keter and Hochma, each having ten Sefirot. And this operates in them both in the inner vessels — namely in the aspect of the Partzuf itself — and in the hairs of the head, which are the surroundings of the Galgalta, and in the hairs of the beard, which are surroundings from the aspect of the Sealed Brain. Likewise in the inner light within the inner vessels of the hairs of the head and the beard, and in the surrounding light within the inner vessels of the hairs of the head and the beard. For even in the hairs, which are discerned permanently as surrounding vessels, the aspect of the inner is discerned in them — but only at the time of the ascent of the Partzufim, when Arich Anpin ascends to Atik, are the hairs then discerned as the aspects of inner vessels, as above, Page 302, Item 12. (Page 390, Item 194).
